contexts.title: Maple Court Apartments - resident notice, fall building works
contexts.text:
MAPLE COURT APARTMENTS - RESIDENT NOTICE
Issued September 28, 2026 by the Management Office, 410 Alder Street

Dear residents,

This notice covers building work planned for October and November, plus a few reminders about payments and common areas. Please keep it for reference.

1. Water shutoff
The water supply to all units will be shut off on Wednesday, October 14, from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. while the plumbing contractor replaces the main riser valve on the ground floor. Please fill containers the night before if you need water during that window. When service returns, run your cold tap for two to three minutes to clear any discoloured water. If water has not returned by 2:00 p.m., call the office.

2. Elevator modernization
The passenger elevator will be out of service from Monday, October 19 through Friday, November 6 while the cab, controls and doors are replaced. The freight elevator is not available to residents during this period. Residents who need mobility assistance during the elevator work should contact the office by October 9 so we can arrange help with groceries and deliveries. Large deliveries and move-ins will not be scheduled during these three weeks.

3. Parking permits
Annual parking permits expire on October 31. Renewal costs $45 per vehicle and can be completed through the resident portal or at the office. Vehicles without a current permit after November 7 may be towed at the owner's expense. Guest parking is limited to 48 hours per visit; guests must display a paper pass available from the office.

4. Rent payments
Rent is due on the 1st of each month. A late fee of $75 applies if rent has not been received by the end of the 5th. Payments through the resident portal by bank transfer (ACH) have no processing fee. Card payments are accepted but carry a 2.5% processing fee charged by the payment provider. Cash is not accepted at the office.

5. Package room
The package room on the lobby level is open from 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. daily. Packages not collected within 10 days will be returned to the carrier. Perishable deliveries should be picked up the same day.

6. Pest inspection
Our pest control vendor will carry out a routine inspection of all kitchens and bathrooms on Tuesday, October 27, between 8:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. You do not need to be home. Please clear the area under your kitchen sink.

7. Quiet hours and common areas
Quiet hours are 10:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m. The rooftop terrace closes for the season on November 1. The bike storage room is currently full; ask the office to join the waitlist.

8. Lease renewals
Residents whose leases end in the coming months will receive a renewal offer at least 60 days before the lease end date. If you have not received yours by then, please contact the office.

Office hours are Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. The property manager is Dana Okafor. For after-hours emergencies such as flooding or no heat, call the emergency line listed on the back of your unit door.

Thank you for your patience while we complete these improvements.

Maple Court Management Office

contexts.title: Riverbend Family Clinic - preparing for your annual physical
contexts.text:
RIVERBEND FAMILY CLINIC
Preparing for Your Annual Physical

Thank you for booking your annual physical with Riverbend Family Clinic. This sheet explains how to prepare so your visit runs smoothly. Your visit will be with Dr. Hollis Varga or a member of her care team.

Before your visit
- If your provider ordered fasting bloodwork (such as a lipid panel or fasting glucose), do not eat or drink anything except water for 10 hours before your appointment. Please avoid coffee, including black coffee, and chewing gum during the fasting period. Take your usual medications with water unless your provider has told you otherwise.
- Complete the health history questionnaire in the patient portal at least 2 days before your visit. If you cannot use the portal, arrive 30 minutes early to fill it in on paper.
- Make a list of every medication, vitamin and supplement you take, including the dose.

What to bring
- Photo ID and your current insurance card.
- Your medication list.
- Glasses or hearing aids if you use them.
- Any home blood pressure readings from the last month.

Arriving
Please arrive 15 minutes before your appointment time to check in. If you are more than 15 minutes late, we may need to reschedule you. Parking is available in Lot B behind the building; bring your ticket to the front desk for 2 hours of free validated parking. Street parking on Weller Avenue is metered.

During your visit
Your visit includes a review of your history, vital signs, a physical exam, and any screenings recommended for your age. Flu shots are available at no extra charge during your physical from October through March while supplies last. If you have a specific concern, mention it at check-in so enough time can be set aside; a separate appointment may be needed for complex issues.

After your visit
Lab results are posted to the patient portal, usually within 3 business days. Your provider will message you if anything needs follow-up. Normal results may be posted without a personal note. Follow-up visits can often be done by telehealth.

Cancellations
We ask for at least 24 hours notice if you need to cancel or reschedule. Appointments missed or cancelled with less than 24 hours notice are subject to a $40 missed-appointment fee, which is not covered by insurance.

Billing
Most insurance plans cover one preventive physical per year at no cost to you. Additional services discussed or treated during the visit, such as a new problem or a chronic condition review, may be billed separately and may involve a copay. Questions about coverage should be directed to your insurance company; our billing office can provide the procedure codes.

Front desk hours: Monday to Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.; Saturday, 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m.

contexts.title: Harbor & Pine customer experience team offsite - planning notes
contexts.text:
HARBOR & PINE - CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE TEAM OFFSITE
Planning notes, owner: Priya Nandakumar (updated September 29)

When and where
Thursday, November 12, 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
The Linden Room, Corbett Street Library Annex, 2nd floor, 118 Corbett Street.
Doors open at 9:00 a.m. for coffee. We start at 9:30 sharp.
Remote teammates can join the morning sessions by video; the link will be in the calendar invite. The afternoon planning block is in-person only.

Purpose
Agree on the team's top 3 priorities for Q1, reset how we hand off escalations between the phone and email queues, and spend some unstructured time together. This is not a performance review day.

Agenda
9:30 - Welcome and ground rules (Priya)
10:00 - Retro on Q3 and Q4: what worked, what didn't (facilitated by Tomasz Weller)
11:15 - Break
11:30 - Escalation handoff workshop (Janelle Ortiz)
12:15 - Lunch, catered by Tamarind Kitchen
1:30 - Q1 planning block (no-laptop session; bring a notebook)
3:00 - Break
3:15 - Commitments and owners
4:00 - Wrap-up and feedback
4:30 - Optional: bowling at Lucky Lanes, two blocks away (team pays for lanes; drinks are on you)

Food
Lunch is a buffet with vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options. If you have an allergy or other dietary need, fill in the dietary form linked in the invite by Thursday, November 5. After that date we cannot guarantee a separate meal. Coffee, tea and snacks are provided all day.

Budget
Total budget is $1,800, covering the room ($450), catering ($950), bowling lanes ($200) and supplies ($200). Anything outside these lines needs Priya's approval in advance.

Travel
Most of us are local. If you drive, mileage is reimbursed at 0.62 per mile through the usual expense form; submit within 30 days. The annex has a small lot that fills up by 9:00 a.m.; the city garage on Pell Street is the backup and is not reimbursed. Anyone travelling from the Westbrook office can book the 7:40 a.m. train; tickets are reimbursed.

What to bring
A notebook and pen, one example of an escalation that went badly and one that went well (anonymised), and your honest opinion.

Coverage
The support queues stay open that day. Ravi and Min-jung are covering phones and are joining by video for the morning only. Please set your status to out of office.

Questions go to Priya in the team channel.

contexts.title: Sourdough starter feeding schedule
contexts.text:
SOURDOUGH STARTER - FEEDING SCHEDULE

Day 1: Mix 50 g whole wheat flour with 50 g lukewarm water in a clean jar. Cover loosely and leave at room temperature, ideally 24 to 26 C.

Day 2: You may see a few bubbles or nothing at all. Both are normal. Leave it alone.

Days 3 to 6: Once a day, discard all but 50 g of the starter, then add 50 g flour (half whole wheat, half white) and 50 g water. Stir well and mark the level on the jar with a rubber band.

Days 7 onward: Switch to two feedings a day, about 12 hours apart. A healthy starter should roughly double within 4 to 8 hours of feeding and smell pleasantly sour, like yogurt.

Troubleshooting
- Grey liquid on top ("hooch") means it is hungry. Pour it off and feed.
- No rise after day 10: move it somewhere warmer and use more whole wheat flour.
- Pink or orange streaks: throw it out and start again.

Storage
Once established, keep it in the fridge and feed once a week. Take it out the night before baking and give it two room-temperature feedings before mixing dough.

contexts.title: Tallpine Hiking Club newsletter - October trail conditions
contexts.text:
TALLPINE HIKING CLUB - OCTOBER NEWSLETTER

Trail conditions
The Ridgeback Loop reopened after the September washout, but the lower creek crossing is still slippery; poles recommended. The Cedar Falls spur is closed until further notice while the footbridge is rebuilt. Hemlock Meadow is dry and in good shape.

Upcoming group hikes
- Saturday, October 10: Ridgeback Loop, 7.4 miles, moderate. Meet at the north trailhead at 8:00 a.m. Leader: Gus Almeida.
- Sunday, October 18: Hemlock Meadow family walk, 3 miles, easy. Dogs on leash welcome.
- Saturday, October 31: Full moon night hike, 4 miles. Headlamps required. Limited to 15 people; sign up on the club board.

Club notes
Annual dues of $30 are due by December 1. The gear library now has two extra-large rain shells and a set of microspikes available to borrow. Please return borrowed items within one week.

Reminder: hunting season opens October 15 on the state land bordering the east trails. Wear blaze orange if you hike there.

contexts.title: Brightline Home Renovations - quote Q-2291, hall bathroom remodel
contexts.text:
BRIGHTLINE HOME RENOVATIONS
Quote Q-2291 - Hall bathroom remodel
Prepared for: homeowner, 27 Birchwood Lane
Prepared by: Sam Ferreira, project lead
Date: September 24, 2026

Summary
Full remodel of the hall bathroom: remove existing tub and tile, install walk-in shower, new vanity, toilet, flooring, lighting and exhaust fan. Quoted total: $14,200, including materials, labor, disposal and permit.

Schedule
Start date: Monday, October 12. Estimated duration: 3 weeks.

Line items
Demolition and disposal - $1,350
Plumbing rough-in and fixtures - $3,900
Walk-in shower, tile and glass - $5,200
Vanity, toilet and hardware - $2,300
Flooring - $1,200
Electrical, lighting and fan - $1,100
Paint and finish - $600
Line item total: $15,650

Payment terms
A deposit of 30% is due on signing to reserve the start date. The balance is due in two installments: 40% at completion of rough-in and the remainder at final walkthrough. For this project the deposit is $5,000.

Permits
Brightline pulls the building permit on your behalf. Permit fees are billed separately at cost, typically $250 to $400 depending on the city.

Warranty
All workmanship carries a 2-year warranty from the completion date. Manufacturer warranties apply to fixtures.

Timeline notes
Work begins October 19 pending tile delivery. Most bathrooms of this size take approximately 5 weeks, including inspection. Water to the bathroom will be off for most of the project; the rest of the house stays connected.

Terms
This quote is valid for 30 days. Changes after signing are handled by written change order. Workmanship warranty: 12-month on labor, excluding misuse and normal wear.

Questions: Sam Ferreira, project lead.
contexts.notes: Contradictions: summary total $14,200 vs line item total $15,650; summary says permit included vs Permits section says permit fees billed separately ($250-$400); start date Monday, October 12 vs 'Work begins October 19'; duration 3 weeks vs approximately 5 weeks; deposit 30% (= $4,260 of $14,200 or $4,695 of $15,650) vs stated deposit $5,000; workmanship warranty 2-year vs 12-month on labor.
